description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. A second run changes nothing and a one-off prune runs. The safety check skips the whole prune, from a prune-now and from the timer's service, when a container with an unless-stopped policy is stopped or a required container is missing, and lets it run once they are fine. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2.

steps.label: Record daemon.json as it was before the component
steps.run: mkdir -p /etc/docker; if [ -s /etc/docker/daemon.json ]; then cp /etc/docker/daemon.json /tmp/tc-before.json; else echo '{}' > /tmp/tc-before.json; fi; cat /tmp/tc-before.json

steps.label: Report mode
Report mode changed nothing
Apply
daemon.json carries the limits
Every key that was already there is unchanged
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open('/tmp/tc-before.json')); b=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); bad=[k for k in a if b.get(k)!=a[k] and k not in ('log-opts','builder')]; print('changed:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

steps.label: dockerd accepts the new file
Prune timer enabled and scheduled
steps.run: systemctl is-enabled tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl is-active tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl list-timers tc-docker-prune.timer --no-pager

steps.label: Prune script has an age filter and never prunes volumes
Second run changes nothing
One-off prune
The prune service itself runs
steps.run: systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service && systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value

steps.label: Settings file carries the age
A container meant to run (unless-stopped) is stopped
steps.run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $d/bin; cp /bin/sleep $d/bin/; for l in $(ldd /bin/sleep | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p $d$(dirname $l); cp $l $d$l; done; tar -C $d -c . | docker import - tc-test-sleep:1; docker run -d --name tc-web --restart unless-stopped tc-test-sleep:1 /bin/sleep 3600; docker stop -t 1 tc-web; docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.label: Prune-now is skipped by the safety check
The timer's service is skipped too, and shows as failed
steps.run: systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 30 --no-pager

steps.label: Start it again
steps.run: docker start tc-web && docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' tc-web

steps.label: A missing required container skips the prune
Required container running: prune goes ahead
Required list saved for the weekly timer
Refuses a container name with shell characters
Refuses a bad log size
Refuses a prune age under 24 hours
Refuses a schedule systemd cannot parse
After a Docker restart, a new container gets max-size 10m
steps.run: systemctl restart docker && docker run --rm -d --name tc-logtest alpine sleep 30 && docker inspect tc-logtest --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}'

steps.label: Host without Docker says so and exits 0
